name: Five-Bay Bookshelf
description: Tall bookshelf, 800 x 300 x 1800 mm: 18 mm carcass, four fixed shelves on a ~360 mm pitch making five bays, closed with a 12 mm back panel.

steps.instruction: Create the bookshelf carcass: two side panels 18 mm thick, 300 mm deep and 1800 mm tall at X=+/-391 (outer faces at +/-400), joined by a bottom panel (Z=0 to 18) and a top panel (Z=1782 to 1800), each 764 x 300 x 18 mm, fused into one frame centered in X and Y.

transcript.user_prompt: Let's build a tall bookshelf, 800 mm wide, 300 mm deep and 1800 mm tall overall, centered in X and Y with its base on Z=0. Create the carcass: two side panels 18 mm thick and 300 mm deep running the full 1800 mm height at X=+/-391 (outer faces at +/-400), a bottom panel 764 x 300 x 18 mm between them from Z=0 to Z=18, and a matching top panel from Z=1782 to Z=1800, all fused into one frame.
transcript.assistant_message: The carcass frame is up: full-height 18 mm sides at +/-400 mm, closed by the 764 mm bottom and top panels - an 800 x 300 x 1800 mm open box.

steps.instruction: Add four fixed shelves, each 764 x 300 x 18 mm spanning between the side panels, with their undersides at Z=370, 730, 1090 and 1450.

transcript.user_prompt: Divide it into five bays: add four fixed shelves, each 764 x 300 x 18 mm spanning the full depth between the side panels, with their undersides at Z=370, Z=730, Z=1090 and Z=1450 - roughly a 360 mm pitch for books.
transcript.assistant_message: Four shelves are in at 370, 730, 1090 and 1450 mm, splitting the case into five bays of book-friendly height.

steps.instruction: Add a back panel 800 mm wide, 1800 mm tall and 12 mm thick, flush with the back face (Y=138 to Y=150), covering the whole back.

transcript.user_prompt: Close the back: add a 12 mm back panel covering the full 800 x 1800 mm back face, flush with the rear edges (spanning Y=138 to Y=150).
transcript.assistant_message: The 12 mm back panel now closes the case - every bay is backed, and the shelf reads as one rigid 800 x 300 x 1800 mm unit.
